Hello, I’m Jonáš Gaigr.
I am an ecologist and conservationist at the Department of Biodiversity Monitoring, Nature Conservation Agency of the Czech Republic. I work on systemic change in the monitoring and evaluation methods used to assess the state of species and habitats within the Natura 2000 network and key umbrella species in Czechia.
🔭 My work centres on building a system for the condition evaluation of species and habitats in Czechia across scales, developed in the host_naturecz repository.
📦 I develop ndopred, an R package that turns occurrence records from NDOP (Nálezová databáze ochrany přírody, the Agency’s species occurrence database) into IUCN Red List metrics and categories for national and regional Red List work. It calculates extent of occurrence, area of occupancy, and population trends following the IUCN criteria (v3.1) and the 2024 guidelines, and ships two Shiny dashboards: one for screening long lists of taxa, one for settling a defensible category taxon by taxon.
🐸 I coordinate the BiodivPond pilot, a transnational pond biodiversity monitoring initiative supported by the Biodiversa+ partnership. If you work on amphibian, bat, or aquatic invertebrate monitoring and conservation in Europe, I’d love to hear from you.
👯 I’m looking to collaborate on exploring biodiversity trends in Czechia, evaluating the condition of protected species, and assessing the impact of conservation interventions.
💩🐞 I also dig into the faunistics of European dung beetles, collecting data on their distribution and abundance, like the occurrence data for Euoniticellus fulvus.

I am an ecologist working on systemic change in monitoring and evaluation methods used to assess the state of species and habitats within the Natura 2000 network and key umbrella species in Czechia. My work includes mainstreaming novel biodiversity monitoring methods, developing and revising monitoring methodologies, producing and maintaining algorithms for data analysis, and transforming information systems to aggregate and share data on Natura 2000 and selected threatened species with conservation authorities and stakeholders.
